newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols stagnant in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols stagnant in thin trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were stagnant on light volume as underlying markets moved very little and many traders were off ahead of the Christmas holiday, dealers said.
"It's a sleeper downstairs," said a derivatives desk manager for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "Most of the locals are out of the pit and there's very little liquidity."
Implied volatilities for CME March and June Eurodollar futures options were virtually unchanged from Friday's closings at around 9.0 and 13.5 percent respectively.

Although traders disliked having any exposure to time-decay, they were also reluctant to sell options aggressively because they would not be receiving a comfortable enough premium due to the historically low implied volatility levels, dealers said.
Trading was also subdued in the Chicago Board of Trade Treasury bond pit as futures bounced off early lows to claw back into positive territory.
"Basically, we're going nowhere," a brokerage firm trader said. He said he saw no sizable option deals today.
Implied volatilities for CBOT February and March T-bond futures options stood little changed at around 9.6 and 9.8 percent respectively.

Traders said there was little reaction to November U.S. personal income and spending data. Income was up 0.5 percent against forecasts for a 0.6 percent rise, while spending was up 0.5 percent against expectations of a 0.3 percent gain.
Trading at both CME and CBOT finishes early on Tuesday and will be closed all day Wednesday for Christmas Day.
